messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Automated rollout (svc-inference v2.4.0) started 15m ago and canary failing healthchecks — 60% of canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Triggering thread and paging oncall. autoscaler observed surge.

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall: maya (primary) -> please acknowledge. Incident ticket created: INC-1234. Severity: P1.

maya: ack'ing. I'm pulling logs now. tagging @raj for runtime context.

raj: on way in. quick question — is this the canary that included the sidecar change for metrics-shim?

elena: yes, that change added an init container that waits for /mnt/config to be mounted, plus a host-affinity tweak to prefer new nodes for the canary.

maya: kubectl get pods -n prod svc-inference-canary -o wide shows many pods stuck in Init:CrashLoopBackOff. Some nodes show NotReady (cordoned earlier for maintenance).

sam: grabbing a pod describe and logs.

sam: ```
kubectl describe pod svc-inference-canary-7f8d9 -n prod
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  2m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned prod/svc-inference-canary-7f8d9 to ip-10-3-45-22
  Warning FailedMount  1m  kubelet            MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "config-dir" : hostPath type check failed: /mnt/config is not a directory
  Warning  BackOff  30s (x3 over 1m)  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed init container
```

sam: init container log: "ERROR: expected directory at /mnt/config, found symlink -> /var/tmp/staging (permissions denied)"

maya: that matches: the hostPath expected directory but our node maintenance script cleaned /mnt/config and left symlink. The affinity change was preferring nodes that had that mount in the baseline image. With cordons and some nodes NotReady, scheduler placed pods on nodes without the dir.

raj: oh — so two interacting factors: init container is strict about hostPath, and affinity reduced scheduling flexibility. With fewer eligible nodes, pods go to bad nodes and crash.

elena: HPA reacted to pod failures and spun up more replicas, making more pods stuck — cascading.

maya: customer impact check: console shows increased 5xx from inference endpoints in eu-west region since rollout. Visibility: ~12% of requests failing, timeout/error budget breached for two customers on dedicated capacity (ids: C-238, C-412). Not global yet.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag for v2 rollout to stop sending traffic to canary, 2) pause/abort rollout and trigger rollback to v2.3.8, 3) cordon the handful of nodes with missing mount so scheduler won't use them, 4) scale HPA min back down after stabilization, 5) postmortem and follow-ups.

raj: agree. I'll flip the kill-switch now (LaunchDarkly flag: inference_canary_v2_traffic -> OFF).

raj: done — flag set to OFF. :white_check_mark: 0 -> 100% traffic diverted from canary.

maya: confirming traffic shift — metrics show canary request rate dropped to near zero. Errors on prod endpoints decreasing but pods still crash (init). Need to stop further canary pod creation.

elena: aborting rollout via deploy tool. Command: ```
./deploy rollback --service svc-inference --to-version 2.3.8 --confirm
```

elena: issued rollback, controller reported rollback started.

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued by elena. Rollback task id: RB-7782. Notify when completed.

sam: I'm cordoning the two nodes missing /mnt/config: ip-10-3-45-22, ip-10-3-46-11. ```
kubectl cordon ip-10-3-45-22
kubectl cordon ip-10-3-46-11
```

sam: cordoned. Also creating a short-lived DaemonSet to ensure /mnt/config has correct permissions on remaining nodes (quick patch): ```
kubectl apply -f fix-mount-perms.yaml
# manifest creates a privileged pod that ensures /mnt/config exists and is dir
```

maya: good. Rolling status: rollback controller indicates 60% of pods restored to 2.3.8 image, remaining still terminating due to init failures on the cordoned nodes but no new canaries spinning up.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-1234 updated: mitigation in progress, P1 -> customer-impacting but contained.

maya: customer comms: outreach to C-238 and C-412 being drafted by support. Need ETA for full recovery. Raj estimate: 15-25 minutes after rollback completes and pods stabilize.

raj: estimate stands — once rollback finishes pods will run without the new init container expectation. HPA scaling will slowly reduce replica churn.

elena: logs show one controller had rate limit on image pull (registry throttling) — we had a backlog and pull retries slowed convergence. Will note in follow-up.

sam: rollback completed. RB-7782: success. All svc-inference replicas now at 2.3.8.

maya: verifying: 200/200 pods Ready, error rate back to baseline in 3 regions (eu-west recovering). Customers C-238 and C-412 notified with update.

elena: immediate RCA (summary): release-v2.4.0 included a hostPath-dependent init container + node-preference affinity. During a routine node maintenance two nodes lost /mnt/config (symlinked), affinity reduced scheduling options, scheduler placed canary pods on nodes without proper hostPath, init containers failed -> CrashLoopBackOff -> HPA churn amplified failures -> partial customer impact.

maya: next-actions (assigned):
- elena: remove hostPath dependency from init (or make it optional) and add mount validation in CI.
- raj: add rollout guard in deploy tooling to require N unaffected nodes with mount present before scheduling hostPath-requiring pods.
- sam: add runbook step to check mounts during maintenance and a pre-drain health check.
- maya: write incident summary and schedule postmortem meeting.

elena: I'll open a PR with the init container fallback (make it exit 0 if mount missing but flag an event). Also add integration test for mount presence.

raj: I'll extend rollout check: if podSpec contains hostPath mounts, require a node-label 'mounts:ok' threshold > 3 in target cluster.

sam: will update maintenance runbook and add a k8s pre-drain hook to validate mounts.

maya: marking resolved for now — system stabilized, rollback completed, customer comms sent. Moving to postmortem. Will update INC-1234 with timeline and action items. :memo: :tada:

deploy-bot: Incident INC-1234: status -> mitigated. Final severity P1 -> mitigated. Please file postmortem within 72 hours.

maya: thanks team. quick kudos to the fast handoff and rollback. We'll keep this blameless and focus on process + test coverage. :heart:
